hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `hrow` only to extract `hKa : conjugate h.K h.a = h.K`, the 7th component of `Row516`, by `obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, -, -, hKa, -⟩ := hrow`. `Row516` is `∃ p f, p.Prime ∧ p ≠ 2 ∧ 1 ≤ f ∧ LieModel … ∧ conjugate h.K h.a = h.K ∧ …`. Its witnesses p, f are unrelated to the theorem's own `{p f}`, and nothing else is taken from it. The same `hKa` follows from `hin : h.a ∈ h.K ⊔ coreActionKernel h.K`. `coreActionKernel J` is defined (UnbalancedLayerSemidihedralTwoComponents.lean) with carrier `{g | g ∈ normalizer (J : Set H) ∧ …}`, so `coreActionKernel h.K ≤ normalizer h.K`. Also `h.K ≤ normalizer h.K`. Hence `h.K ⊔ coreActionKernel h.K ≤ normalizer h.K`, so `h.a ∈ normalizer h.K`. For `a` in the normalizer, `conjugate K a = K.map (MulAut.conj a⁻¹) = K`, since `a⁻¹` is also in the normalizer. So `hKa` can be proved from `hin` alone, and the rest of the proof (`inner_data h hp hp2 hJ hKa hin`, etc.) is unchanged. The statement stays true without `hrow`. I did not check the Lean lemma names for the normalizer step. The reasoning rests on the definition of `coreActionKernel` and on `normalizer` being applied to a `Set` here.
